Thanks James — good questions. Quick answers below and details attached.

Peering vs PrivateLink (summary):
- VPC Peering: simple route-table changes, lower latency, good for high throughput. Requires peering connection and mutual acceptance from both accounts; your team will need to add route table entries for subnets that talk to the Redwood subnets. No additional NLB required.
- PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint): provides stronger isolation (no transitive routing) and is usually what security teams prefer. It requires us to front services with an NLB in our account and for you to create interface endpoints in yours. Slightly higher per-connection operational overhead but often easier to audit.

IP allowlist / egress info:
- For the Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) there is no Redwood-managed egress — egress is controlled by your VPC/NAT.
- For Hosted fallback (if you want to test before Private is ready), we can provide a small set of egress IPs you can allowlist. I attached the checklist which includes the temporary test IPs under the "Hosted fallback" tab.

Attachments (see attached checklist): the checklist walks through required IAM permissions, recommended route-table entries for peering, steps to create interface endpoints, and the temporary egress IP list for Hosted testing.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical sync with Anna (cloud engineer) to review the network diagram and decide peering vs PrivateLink.
- I'll include Rafael on the next thread once we have a sense of capacity/commitment so he can share pricing for Dedicated vs Private.

Proposed times: Tue 16 Mar 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 17 Mar 09:00-10:00 PT. Which works for you?

Best,

Hi James / Anna —

Looping in a bit more technical detail from the infra side so you have what your cloud team will ask for on the sync: 

1) Preferred recommendation: VPC Peering for lowest latency and simplest egress path. Use peering if you expect high sustained throughput for inference traffic.

2) PrivateLink tradeoffs: Excellent for security reviews (no cross-account route-table changes). We front the endpoint with an internal NLB and advertise private IPs. It adds a small latency delta and requires creating interface endpoints in your VPC.

3) IP allowlist specifics: For Hosted fallback, allowlist the following temporary egress IPs (example): 52.11.33.210, 52.11.33.211, 52.11.33.212. For Dedicated/Private deployments, egress is controlled by your VPC; if you need fixed outbound IPs we can provide NAT/transit options as part of a Dedicated setup (Rafael can follow up on procurement/pricing).

4) What we need from you for the tech sync:
- VPC CIDR(s) you plan to use and which subnets are eligible for interface endpoints / peering.
- Your preferred AWS account ID to initiate peering (or confirm if you prefer we provide a PrivateLink service name).
- A contact for your security/compliance reviewer (SOC2).

I've uploaded the network diagram to a shared drive here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-network-diagrams

I'll be on the sync if needed. Rafael - adding you to keep procurement in the loop as we move from evaluation to Dedicated/reserved contract.

Thanks,
